review_evidence: Focused schema, runtime hash, pedagogy quality, and key self-review for eng_c3_ch05 on 2026-07-12
title: Talking Toys
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Follow the toy-shop story
levels.teaching_goal: Track where the story is happening, who enters, and which toy is chosen next.

guided_check.teaching_block: In a toy-shop story, do not jump straight to the toy names. First find the place, then follow who comes in, then connect each child to a toy.
guided_check.passage: The shutters open in a busy market. Wooden toys, board games, balls, and soft toys wait on the shelves.
guided_check.prompt: Where does this story scene begin?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: a story place is usually the answer to 'where'. Here the shelves and toys point to a toy shop.
bridge.passage: A child looks at dolls, trains, and games kept on racks.
bridge.prompt: Which place has dolls, trains, and games on racks?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: rebuild the sequence with three questions: where are we, who enters, and what toy is chosen?
masterclass.passage: First a family enters the shop. The child points to a toy that runs on tracks.
masterclass.prompt: Which toy is the child likely choosing?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now follow a new toy-shop clue without hints.
independent_check.passage: A boy walks past the dolls and board games. He stops at the toy that has wheels and coaches.
independent_check.prompt: Which toy does the boy choose?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply the same clue-tracking strategy at a school exhibition: identify the place, follow the visitor, and connect the final action to the object chosen.
transfer_check.passage: At the class craft fair, Nila passes clay pots and bead bracelets. She stops where a wooden figure moves when strings are pulled.

levels.title: Use toy words from context
levels.focus: use context to understand a word
levels.teaching_goal: Use nearby clues to understand toy vocabulary instead of memorising a list.

guided_check.teaching_block: A toy word becomes easier when you read the clue around it. If a toy can wear a frock and sit on a shelf, it may be a doll.
guided_check.passage: The toy with a pink frock and two ribbons sat beside a wooden elephant.
guided_check.prompt: Which toy is described by the pink frock clue?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: match the clue to the toy. Frock and ribbons describe a doll, not a ball or a kite.
bridge.passage: The child held the toy like a baby and combed its hair.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: some toys are chosen by how they are played with. Small round glass balls used in a game are marbles.
masterclass.passage: Two friends knelt on the floor and rolled small round balls in a game.
masterclass.prompt: Which toy word fits the clue?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now use the action clue without help.
independent_check.passage: The children rolled small round balls and tried to hit one with another.
independent_check.prompt: Which toy are they playing with?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Move the context clue strategy beyond a toy shop. Use what an object does, not its location, to name it.
transfer_check.passage: During games period, Sana spins a round disc on a pointed end. It turns quickly before falling on its side.

levels.title: Add describing words
levels.teaching_goal: Connect a describing word to the naming word it tells more about.

guided_check.teaching_block: A describing word tells more about a naming word. In 'red top', red tells what kind of top it is.
guided_check.passage: The child picked a red top from the shelf.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: first find the naming word. Then ask, 'What kind?' The answer is the describing word.
bridge.passage: The soft bear sat near the green train.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: a noun names the toy; a describing word adds detail. Use both to make the picture clearer.
masterclass.prompt: Which phrase uses the describing word correctly?

independent_check.teaching_block: Choose details that help a reader picture a new toy, then put them in a complete sentence.
independent_check.passage: Toy: horse. Details: shiny, wooden. Action: stands by the window.
independent_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence describing the horse.

concept_slots.description: Names the horse.
Uses at least one given describing word.
States where the horse stands.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the noun-and-description strategy for a real classroom object. Include enough detail for a listener to identify it.
transfer_check.passage: Object: school bag. Details: blue, heavy. Place: under Rehan's desk.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence describing the bag.

concept_slots.description: Names the bag.
Uses blue or heavy as a describing word.
Gives the location under Rehan's desk.

levels.title: Make plural toy words
levels.teaching_goal: Use s and es endings to show more than one toy or object.

guided_check.teaching_block: A plural word means more than one. For many words, add s: one toy, two toys.
guided_check.passage: One toy is on the table. Many toys are in the basket.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: if the word ends with x, add es. One box becomes boxes.
bridge.passage: One box has blocks. Three boxes have toy cars.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: choose the ending by the word. Simple toy words often take s. Words ending in x, ch, sh, or s often take es.
masterclass.passage: One brush is beside the puppet. Two brushes are beside the paints.

independent_check.teaching_block: Decide whether the ending needs s or es, then form the new plural without choices.
independent_check.passage: One bench holds a toy drum. Three of these seats hold painted tops.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the plural rule to a picnic list. Listen to the final sound before choosing s or es.
transfer_check.passage: One dish has fruit. Four more are ready for sandwiches.

levels.title: Order making steps
levels.teaching_goal: Use sequence words to explain the order of making something.

guided_check.teaching_block: Making activities need order. Words like first, next, then, and finally help a reader follow each step.
guided_check.passage: First, fold the paper. Next, tie the thread. Finally, fly the kite.
guided_check.prompt: Which word tells the first step?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: the first step starts the work; finally tells the last step.
bridge.passage: First, draw a face. Next, colour it. Finally, attach a handle.
bridge.prompt: Which word tells the last step?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: process order is not only about memory. Ask what must happen before the next step can work.
masterclass.passage: A child cuts the puppet shape before colouring the face.

independent_check.teaching_block: Build the whole instruction from an unseen set of ordered steps. Keep the action order unchanged.
independent_check.passage: Steps: wash the jar / dry it / add coloured paper stars.
independent_check.prompt: Write the three steps in order using first, next, and finally.
accepted_answers: first wash the jar next dry it finally add coloured paper stars
first, wash the jar. next, dry it. finally, add coloured paper stars.
first wash the jar, next dry it, and finally add coloured paper stars

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use sequence language to explain a classroom routine instead of making a toy. Include all actions in a useful order.
transfer_check.passage: Routine: choose a library book / write its number / place it in your bag.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one or more complete sentences giving the routine in order.

concept_slots.description: Starts by choosing a library book.
Then tells the reader to write the book number.
Ends by placing the book in the bag.
any_of: finally place it in your bag
place the book in the bag

items.passage: After closing time, a tin robot taps the shelf and a cloth rabbit whispers back. Soon every toy joins their midnight talk.
items.prompt: What is the paragraph mainly about?
options: toys talking after the shop closes
accepted_answers: toys talking after the shop closes

items.passage: A wooden train boasts that it is fastest. The spinning top reminds it that every toy is good at a different game.
items.prompt: What lesson is the main idea?
accepted_answers: each toy is good at something different

items.passage: Ira winds the key on a metal bird. Its wings flap three times before it becomes still.
items.prompt: What happens after Ira winds the key?

items.passage: The puppet bows when Aman pulls the front string, but it lifts one arm when he pulls the side string.
items.prompt: Which string makes the puppet lift an arm?

items.passage: The player strikes its round skin with two sticks, and a deep beat fills the room.
items.prompt: Which toy instrument fits the clue?

items.passage: Strings from the dancer's hands control the little cloth figure on a stage.
items.prompt: Name the figure.

items.passage: The ___ scooter stood beside the door.
items.prompt: Choose the describing word.

items.passage: One watch is broken. Two ___ still tick.
items.prompt: Write the plural of watch.

items.passage: Object card: red fire engine | long ladder | parked beside the dollhouse.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence describing the fire engine.

concept_slots.description: Names the fire engine.
Uses red or long as a describing word.
Gives its place beside the dollhouse.

items.passage: Object card: tiny green kite | silver tail | hanging above the cupboard.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence that helps a reader picture the kite.

concept_slots.description: Names the kite.
Uses at least one given detail.
Gives its place above the cupboard.

items.passage: One fox toy sits upright. Three more are packed in a carton.
items.prompt: Write the plural of fox.

items.passage: One shelf is low. Two higher ones display puzzles.
items.prompt: Write the plural of shelf.

items.passage: Steps: press the clay flat / cut a star / leave it to dry.
items.prompt: Which action must happen before the star can dry?

items.passage: Words: finally / display / the / model / we
items.prompt: Put the words in order.

items.passage: Mohan repairs the loose wheel before racing the toy car.
items.prompt: Why does he repair the wheel first?

concept_slots.description: Mentions the loose wheel or need for repair.
Explains that the car can race, roll, or work safely after repair.

items.passage: Zoya gives the younger children cloth balls instead of hard wooden ones for an indoor game.
items.prompt: Explain her choice.

concept_slots.description: Mentions cloth or soft balls.
Gives a sensible indoor safety reason.

items.passage: The wind-up mouse bumps into a cup, turns around, and continues across the table.
items.prompt: Which event happens last?

items.passage: A silent toy cannot make a sound. This one rings when it is shaken.
items.prompt: Which word best describes this toy?

items.passage: Plan: collect clean cartons / paint them / build a toy-town street.
items.prompt: Write the plan in order with sequence words.

concept_slots.description: Begins by collecting clean cartons.
Places painting after collecting.
Ends by building the street.

items.passage: The toys argue about who should lead the parade. The small whistle listens to every idea and suggests that they take turns. The argument ends.
items.prompt: State the main idea and why the whistle's plan works.

concept_slots.description: Identifies taking turns as the solution or main idea.
Explains that taking turns is fair or ends the argument.
